sentences: A man, probably the Italian merchant Giovanni Arnolfini, who worked in Bruges, stands beside his wife in their room.
Look into the convex mirror on the back wall and you see the couple from behind, plus two figures entering through the doorway: exactly where we are standing.
Above the mirror, a Latin signature reads "Jan van Eyck was here.
1434," as if the painter were a witness to the scene.
The mirror's frame holds tiny roundels, each about half a fingernail wide, painted with scenes of Christ's Passion.
The woman is not pregnant; her full silhouette comes from gathering up her heavy skirts, as fashion then required.
Van Eyck built all of this out of thin, glowing layers of oil glaze.
